question: Which canonical text, editing and syntax-presentation contract should native code blocks use?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 24. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Code content is one canonical newline-bearing Text per code block; syntax tokens are transient decorations, never marks or persisted data.
Native full-DOM editing, static/RSC rendering and an optional bounded-DOM CodeMirror view share canonical text, history, selection and neutral decorations.
Insert/upsert construct schema-valid code nodes and keep code-specific empty-block reuse and selection policy.
The package syntax reader never mutates a caller-supplied highlighter; copied kits own grammar registration and product policy such as JSON formatting.
Plate owns the code feature; Plite owns the external-text slot and canonical change mapping.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-22 audit's 13-group census, the implementation and demo-closure execution records, and the 2026-09-30 static-preview execution's highlight reuse claim. Rechecked on the live tree: BaseCodeBlockPlugin insertion, tab, highlight read and commit cleanup; the copied code-block, code-block-lowlight, code-block-static and code-block-codemirror items and the CodeMirror demo; consumer greps for read/update capabilities; docs claims. All inspected code-block source is committed (git status clean). No test, browser or bundle run.
summary: The job is one newline-bearing Text per code block, edited natively or through an optional CodeMirror external-text view, with transient syntax paint that never enters the document. Live BaseCodeBlockPlugin constructs code nodes with tx.schema.create, keeps code-specific insert and upsert policy, reads only the supplied Lowlight instance, and its tab command excludes an untouched endpoint line. The copied kit registers browser-safe Python at resource construction and owns JSON formatting as one canonical update. The strongest replacement lanes still lose (CodeMirror as sole renderer, deleting native projection, a shared code-text recipe, an incremental native parser), because native, static and full-DOM consumers keep independent jobs and no matched parser benchmark exists. What remains is small. The copied CodeMirror item still imports code-block.tsx, whose module-level createCodeBlockLowlight() loads every Lowlight grammar, an unmeasured bundle cost the earlier review already deferred. read.entry and read.indentDepth have no production caller, and the English insert() docs and Chinese plugin-components/code-block docs are stale. None of these changes the contract.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted design wins. Every Pursue target from 2026-09-22 is in live source, and no lane below beats it.
Make CodeMirror the sole renderer and delete native syntax projection: Stop; static/RSC, full-DOM native editing and mixed views keep independent jobs.
Move parsing or input ownership for code into Plite: Stop; the narrow external-text slot already carries canonical changes, and syntax is Plate/registry product paint.

Replacing Lowlight with one incremental native parser is not selected. No matched whole-operation, language or SSR benchmark exists, so it stays an unaccepted alternative rather than an evidence gap that decides this unit.

Splitting the copied CodeMirror item from the Lowlight-initializing native module is a bounded registry cleanup whose value is a bundle number nobody has measured. It does not change the code contract and stays deferred.
Deleting the unused read helpers (entry, indentDepth) and resetBlock in favor of toggle is a P3 cleanup of public names with no production caller impact, too small to reopen the unit.
proofLimits: Source inspection only. No unit, browser, IME, assistive-technology or packed-artifact run; no bundle measurement of the Lowlight-in-CodeMirror cost; no performance comparison. Browser behavior rests on the 2026-09-22 demo closure and 2026-09-30 execution records, which are stale-bound to earlier source fingerprints. Whether retyping an empty code block to a paragraph leaves a stale language property was not checked.
